idea-plugin.name: ADP: A Different Perspective
idea-plugin.description:
Visual tools for the files you already keep in your project. ADP (A Different Perspective) opens a FreeMind mind map or a draw.io diagram as a picture you can work in, right inside your IDE, and writes every change straight back to the file. Each tool is tuned for one kind of document rather than being a general drawing canvas, so it keeps everything it does not show exactly as it was.

Highlights

  • Your files stay yours. Each tool reads and writes the plain file, so it diffs cleanly, lives in version control and can be edited by hand, by a colleague in another tool or by an AI assistant at the same time.
  • Only what you changed is changed. An edit rewrites just the part of the file it concerns. A file saved without edits stays byte for byte the same.
  • Feels like the IDE. Every change is one named step of Edit | Undo, shared with the text editor; the tab shows when the file is modified, and saving works as for any other file.
  • Text and picture side by side. The tool and the IDE's text editor work on the same document: type in one and the other follows.
  • Works offline. The plug-in makes no network calls and needs no account and nothing else installed.

Mind maps (.mm)

FreeMind mind maps open as a map drawn around its root, with branches on their own side, folding, arrow links, icons, colours, fonts, links and notes.

  • Add, rename, delete, move and drag nodes, and fold branches, from the keyboard or the context menu.
  • The Structure tool window lists the node tree, for quick navigation in large maps.
  • File | New | FreeMind Mind Map starts a new map.
  • Other files ending in .mm, such as Objective-C++ sources, keep opening as they always did.

draw.io diagrams (.drawio)

draw.io diagrams open with their shapes, dashed, curved and orthogonal connections, arrowheads, labels and swimlanes.

  • Add shapes from the toolbox, connect them, and move, resize and delete them.
  • Change fill colours, line styles and labels for one shape or several at once.
  • What the diagram does not show, such as other pages, groups and unfamiliar shapes, is kept as it is.
  • A compressed diagram opens as text, with a note on how to save it uncompressed from draw.io.

Getting started

  1. Open a .mm or .drawio file, or create a mind map with File | New | FreeMind Mind Map.
  2. Use the ADP Toolbox tool window on the right to add elements: drag an entry onto the canvas, or press Enter to add it in the middle.
  3. Select something and edit it in the ADP Properties tool window, or double-click a text (or press F2) to edit it in place.
  4. Settings | Tools | ADP lists the tools and the files each one opens, and holds the canvas options, such as the opening zoom.

Building your own tools

Every ADP tool is described in a tool description. Files with the .atd extension get live problem checking, completion, navigation, rename and formatting in every IDE with language server support.

More

ADP is also available for Visual Studio Code and as an application of its own. Read more at etalii.net/adp, and send questions, ideas and bug reports to the issue tracker. Free and open source under the Apache License 2.0.
